A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SAM-CP and provide readable methods, equations, experiments, figures, tables, and appendices. Their retained and revised material can be reliably matched despite reorganization and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original SAM-CP segmentation results on COCO, ADE20K, and Cityscapes, together with component ablations and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds Pascal Part evaluation, SAM2 transfer and timing experiments, and qualitative camouflage segmentation results.

M1.justification: V2 adds limited inference adaptations: cropping and enlarging regions for additional SAM calls, and dynamically adding denser point prompts to recover small objects (Sections 4.5–4.6). The core composable prompts, affinity decoder, losses, and denoising strategy remain; removing the denoising appendix does not establish removal of that training component.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained COCO, ADE20K, and Cityscapes coverage, v2 evaluates part segmentation on Pascal Part and demonstrates camouflage segmentation on COD10K (Table 10 and Figure 12). These introduce finer semantic granularity and a distinct visual domain, rather than merely additional configurations of existing benchmarks.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds OpenSeeD, HIPIE, CLIPSelf, and FrozenSeg. New appendix Tables 13–15 compare against OVSAM, Prompt Segment Anything, SEEM, and Semantic-SAM, including a reproduced Semantic-SAM result. These substantially expand evaluated comparators; Semantic-SAM was previously cited but not included in these comparisons.

E3.justification: V2 introduces part-only versus part-and-general training comparisons, component-level inference timing on an RTX 4090, and transfer of trained CP weights to SAM2 without retraining. These substantially extend the evaluation design. The retained main benchmark splits, preprocessing, and training budgets are unchanged; the additions do not establish rerunning those experiments.

E4.justification: V2 adds analyses of joint part/general training, SAM2 transfer and efficiency, camouflage generalization, classification through patch aggregation, and recovery through denser prompts or additional SAM calls. The original component and matching analyses remain, with v1's matching-threshold ablation relocated to v2 Appendix C.1 and Table 12.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests. The new results retain the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Original SAM-CP scores in Tables 1–2 remain unchanged, while substantial new results appear: Pascal Part mAP of 13.7/13.6 and SAM2-CP at 27.9 PQ and 1.79 seconds/image (Tables 10–11). Added HIPIE results report 19.0 AP versus SAM-CP's unchanged 17.0 on COCO→ADE20K. Table 4 also fills the previously blank without-QE open-domain AP cell with 16.5.

T1.justification: The affinity and supervision definitions, Equations 1–2, complexity discussion, and Algorithm 1 are retained. New explanations and illustrations do not introduce revised mathematical reasoning, formal assumptions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: two composable prompts, a unified affinity framework, versatile segmentation, and state-of-the-art open-vocabulary performance. The new experiments extend support without materially redefining these core claims.

C2.justification: V2 explains how aggregating ambiguous patches supplies enough context for classification and qualifies the missing-object limitation with denser prompting (Section 4.6). It also identifies reliance on color rather than semantics as a limitation for part segmentation. These refine the existing interpretation that SAM patch quality constrains SAM-CP.

D1.justification: V2 documents RTX 4090 timing and SAM2 transfer without retraining, but removes v1 Appendix A.3's denoising implementation explanation. Appendix B.4 replaces a repository link with a supplementary code.zip instruction, while the abstract explicitly states code release. These change documentation and access instructions; actual external availability is not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: V2 adds recent references such as FrozenSeg, CLIPSelf, OpenSeeD, HIPIE, and Semantic-aware SAM, plus appendix positioning against additional SAM-related methods. The original foundation-model, affinity, and detector-dependence narrative remains largely intact; bibliographic publication updates do not constitute new cited works.

P1.justification: Most original prose remains. V2 moves inference into the experiments section and the matching-threshold discussion into Appendix C, expands local supervision explanations, and subdivides the discussion. Author information, acknowledgments, terminology, and citation presentation also receive localized edits.

P2.justification: V2 adopts the ICLR layout, redraws Figure 2, expands the affinity-label illustration, adds several experimental figures and tables, and removes v1's Figure 5 COCO montage. Existing threshold results and appendix galleries are relocated or resized. These substantially change the visual presentation beyond numerical updates and renumbering.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens practical validation through timing and SAM2 transfer experiments, tests previously prospective part segmentation, and adds relevant SAM-based comparisons. These provide useful evidence beyond v1. The gains are tempered by sparse protocols for the new tasks, removal of denoising details, and overbroad comparison prose: Section 4.3 claims advantages over FrozenSeg for metrics and transfer directions absent from Table 1. Overall, the paper improves, but the added evidence remains unevenly documented.
